relationships.title: Presbytery authority to judge theonomy as heresy under WCF 19-4

occurrences.excerpt: The CCB advised that a presbytery retains the right to examine and judge a man heretical on WCF 19-4 grounds, provided the error is demonstrated by specific evidence.

relationships.title: Jeffrey M. Black v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: …interpretation and the issues of the Sabbath (WCF 21-8) and theonomy (WCF 19-4).

metadata.synopsis: Black challenged Presbytery’s handling of his complaint and its ruling that a licentiate’s non-24-hour creation-day view was not an exception to the Westminster Standards. The SJC denied remand because Presbytery had effectively adjudicated the complaint; the separate objection to proceeding without Black was not first filed below and was administratively out of order. It upheld Presbytery’s ruling that not every non-Calendar-Day view constitutes an exception. Because the record did not identify the licentiate’s precise view, the decision did not determine its acceptability or whether it could be taught.

relationships.title: Jupiter Session vs. Southern Florida Presbytery

occurrences.excerpt: …vote of 30 against, 21 for, and 1 abstention. In particular, TE Slack was read WCF 19-4 and asked to cite an example of Old Testament judicial law that had expired. He stated he was unable to do so (RoC page 25). In denying transfer, Presbytery did grant…

…but did not hear complainants. TE Slack was asked if he was in agreement with WCF 19-4. He answered in the affirmative. He also was asked if he could cite examples of Old Testament judicial law which had expired to confirm his belief that people no longer…

…longer were obligated to keep them except for general equity as set forth in WCF 19-4. He responded that he could think of no specifics and that general equity basically encompassed the judicial law (RoC pages 25 & 26).
